title: Air Starter Harness Retention Revision at the Heat Shield Crossing
abstract: Proposal to change the harness retention where the starter feeder crosses the heat shield, so that the recurring cable tie renewal at engine change is replaced by a supported run to the current retention standard.

sections.reason: The starter feeder is retained across the heat shield by cable ties that are cut at every removal and renewed on installation. Line stations report that the ties are the item most often found broken or displaced at engine change, and that a displaced tie lets the feeder rest on the shield edge. The current retention standard elsewhere on the engine uses a supported clamp and does not have this behaviour. Two operators have asked for the same arrangement here.
sections.description: The proposal replaces the cable tie retention at the shield crossing with the current supported clamp standard, using the clamp already qualified on the lower duct run. The bracket FJD726238-84 that carries the retention point is retained and the fastener set AES139278K3 is unchanged. The heat shield itself and the duct standoffs are not touched, so the change is a retention kit only and no laminate or standoff question arises.
sections.effects: Mass change is negligible. No electrical load change. Interchangeable. The recurring cable tie renewal at engine change disappears and with it the displaced-tie finding. No dispatch, crew or manual content change beyond the removal task illustration.
sections.embodiment_note: Proposal only. If taken forward it would be a bulletin embodied at any engine change, about one hour per engine.
sections.open_points: Not yet analysed. The obvious question is whether a retention change on its own is worth a bulletin, given that the finding line stations actually record at engine change is the standoff fretting rather than the tie.

type_data.production_impact: None proposed; the line will build to the frozen change

title: Air Starter Duct Standoff Alignment and Harness Retention Revision

issue.reason: Scope widened to carry the standoff move onto the delivered shield, and the bracket commonality question with the frozen heat shield change added to the open points.

abstract: Proposal to align the air starter duct standoffs and change the harness retention on aircraft that will not receive the frozen heat shield change, so that the fretting finding is answered on the in-service fleet as well as on the line.

sections.reason: The heat shield obsolescence change is frozen for production and carries a standoff move with it, but it is not offered as a retrofit because the delivered shield remains serviceable for life. That leaves the whole in-service fleet with the standoff and harness arrangement that produces the fretting finding at every engine change, which line stations record and then do nothing about. Three operators have asked what they are supposed to do with a finding that has no action.
sections.description: The proposal takes the standoff move from the frozen change and applies it to the delivered shield, which needs a slightly different bracket because the delivered shield is thicker at the edge, and changes the harness retention in that area to the current cable tie standard. The clamp at the lower duct run is replaced with the current item. The heat shield itself is not touched, so no laminate question arises and the change is a bracket and retention kit only.
sections.effects: Mass change is negligible. No electrical load change. Interchangeable. The finding at engine change should disappear, which removes a recurring inspection report that currently has no disposition. No dispatch, crew or manual content change beyond the removal task illustration.
sections.embodiment_note: Proposal only. If taken forward it would be a bulletin embodied at any engine change, about three hours per engine.
sections.open_points: Not yet analysed. The obvious question is whether this proposal and the frozen change can share one bracket part rather than two, and whether it is worth doing at all on aircraft that will be retired before the next engine change.

type_data.production_impact: None proposed; the line will build to the frozen change
